newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on political tension.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on political tension.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply lower on Wednesday in thin trading amid rising political tension, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 2.03 percent, or 5.20 points, to 251.30 on low all-share turnover of 80 million shekels against 116 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.93 percent lower at 260.14.
"The market is declining but activity is low and there is no panic. There are only few sellers and the positive trend is expected to continue," said Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"The main trigger for today's decline was the worsening political situation. The tension with the Palestinians is preventing the market from rising further," he said.
Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities, said the the market was looking for direction.

"It's difficult to say if today's decline is only a consolidation or the beginning of another negative trend. All the technical indicators show that the trend is still positive but the political uncertainty has a negative impact on trading," Nahum said.

Israeli soldiers wounded 31 Palestinians in renewed clashes in the town of Hebron on Wednesday. The street battles flared a day after the heaviest bloodshed in the West Bank since the crisis began last month.
"The events in Hebron raised the uncertainty and investors do not know where the peace process is going. A breakthrough in peace talks would lead to an immediate recovery of the market," Nahum said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.5 percent to 31,132 agorot on a turnover of 7.2 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which fell 1.75 percent to 545 agorot on volume of 4.7 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.5 percent to 18,845 agorot on turnover of 3.0 million shekels.
